summary: Frank E. Reynolds was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He spent his career at the University of Chicago, serving as Professor from circa 1967 to 2001 and as Emeritus Professor from circa 2001 until 2019.

Frank Ernest Keay worked in Indology and religious studies, earning his B.A. (by 1900) and M.A. (by 1917) from the University of London. He was Principal of Talghari Boys’ School in 1922 and a priest at Bishop Cotton School (1941–1944).
Frank F. Conlon is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Minnesota in 1969. He served as Professor Emeritus at the University of Washington around 2003.

Frank J. Hoffman is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa under Stewart Sutherland, Eliot Deutsch, David J. Kalupahana, Prithwish Neogy, Rama Nath Sharma, and Kashi Nath Upadhyaya.
Frank J. Korom works in religious studies and Indology. He completed graduate studies at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 1990) and served as a professor at Boston University (attested 2005).

Frank Lee Woodward was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar educated at Christ's Hospital and Sidney Sussex College. He taught at several schools, served as Dekan of Mahinda College (1903–1919), and translated Buddhist texts for the Pali Text Society in 1919.

Frank Lillingston worked in religious studies and Indology. He earned his B.A. (~1891–1894) and M.A. (~1894–1898) from Pembroke College and served as Theological Lecturer at Selwyn College from 1897 to 1898.

Frank Raymond Allchin was a scholar of archaeology and Indology who studied at SOAS under K. de B. Codrington. He taught at SOAS (1954–1959) and the University of Cambridge (1959–1989), later working at the Ancient India and Iran Trust.

Frank Walter Nicolson specialized in Indology and other fields. After studying at Mount Allison University and Harvard University, he served as Instructor in Sanskrit at Harvard (1888–1889) and Professor of Latin at Wesleyan University (1913–1934).
Frank Whittingham Skemp was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Manchester (~1897–1900) and at Peterhouse (1903–1904) in preparation for the I.C.S.

Frank-Richard Hamm studied Indology and Tibetology at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring and habilitated there in 1957. He held posts at Hamburg, the Free University of Berlin (chair, 1964), and the University of Bonn (Professor, 1965).

Franklin Edgerton was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He held professorships at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926), Yale University (1926–1953), Harvard University (~1949), and Banaras Hindu University (1953–1954).

Frans Wilhelm Gustaf Hjelt was an Indologist who studied at the University of Helsinki and Uppsala University under Otto Fredrik Tullberg. He held a post at the University of Helsinki in 1844 and served as Rector of Turun Katedraalikoulu (1845–1872).
František Kamarýt was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University, completing his Ph.D. under Josef Zubatý by 1917.

František Čupr was a philosopher and Indologist who completed his Ph.D. at Charles University by 1845. He held a lecturing post at Charles University in 1849 and later taught and served as principal at secondary schools in Prague.

František Šohaj worked in Indology and linguistics. After receiving his Ph.D. from Charles University by 1848, he served there as Professor of Philosophy from 1848 to 1859 before taking a post at Akademické gymnázium v Praze in 1859.

Franz Altheim was a historian and archaeologist of Central Asia and Iran. He earned his Ph.D. and became Privatdozent at Frankfurt, later serving as Professor at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1936) and the Free University of Berlin (1950–1965).

Franz Aubrey Metcalf is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from the University of California, Berkeley (BA), Graduate Theological Union (MA), and the University of Chicago (Ph.D.), and taught at California State University, Los Angeles in 1998.

Franz August Schmölders studied Indology and philosophy at the Universities of Bonn and Paris. He held positions at the University of Bonn, served as Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin (1842), and became Professor at the University of Breslau (1846).

Franz Bernhard was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Göttingen under Ernst Waldschmidt and Werner Thomas, and habilitated at Frankfurt. He held posts at Tübingen, Frankfurt, and as Professor at the University of Hamburg (1966–1971).
